bug_semantics: picklescan's pickle GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL classifier only raises issues_count for names present in the `_unsafe_globals` denylist. At v1.0.3, `_build_scan_result_from_raw_globals` (src/picklescan/scanner.py:389-424) marks denylist hits Dangerous and increments issues_count, but any other known-but-unlisted global is SafetyLevel.Suspicious and is not counted as an issue, so the CLI reports CLEAN. CVE-2026-56315 / first-party GHSA-g38g-8gr9-h9xp is CWE-184: before 1.0.4 that denylist omitted at least uuid._get_command_stdout (subprocess.Popen), _osx_support._read_output/_find_build_tool (os.system), _aix_support._read_cmd_output (os.system), _pyrepl.pager.pipe_pager/tempfile_pager (Popen(shell=True)/os.system), imaplib.IMAP4_stream (Popen(shell=True)), and test.support.script_helper.assert_python_ok (python subprocess). An attacker ships a pickle that REDUCE-calls one of those stdlib functions; scan_pickle_bytes returns issues_count==0 while pickle.loads executes the command. Affected: all published versions <1.0.4 (CVE.org: from 0 before 1.0.4).
flaw_origin: The fail-open denylist was first written in c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e ('Implement Pickle scanner', 2022-09-04/05) as `_suspicious_globals` at src/picklescan/scanner.py:14-23 plus the scan_pickle_bytes loop at :83-88 that increments issues_count only on denylist hits. That first list contained only __builtin__, builtins, webbrowser, httplib, requests.api, aiohttp.client, nt, and posix — not uuid, _osx_support, _aix_support, _pyrepl, imaplib, or test. Immediate parent 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 is boilerplate with no src/picklescan/scanner.py. Later commits renamed the dict to `_unsafe_globals` (f98f9bd) and added other modules for unrelated advisories; git log -S shows the CVE modules first appear in the 1.0.4 fix. The incomplete list is therefore the original first write, not a later regression.
